name: SoftSync
summary: Flexible B2B CRM for small sales teams: records and custom objects, table, pipeline and calendar views, email sync and campaigns, meeting notes and summaries, Autopilot follow-up workflows, and API and MCP access so Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini can work with the CRM directly.
best_for: small B2B sales teams of up to five people who want CRM records, email campaigns, meeting summaries and follow-up automation in one workspace, and who want Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini to work with that CRM directly rather than through a connector marketplace
skip_if: your team will pass five users soon and the jump to $59 per seat breaks the budget; you run high-volume outbound where 1,000 campaign emails per user a month is too tight; or you rely on a library of prebuilt integrations rather than an API and MCP connection
honest_knock:
Pro stops at five team members per workspace. The sixth person does not add a sixth Pro seat; it moves the whole team to Business, which is $59 per seat a month on yearly billing instead of $29. A five-person team on Pro pays $145 a month billed yearly; the same team plus one hire pays $354 on Business, for the same product surface, since the pricing page says both paid plans carry the same core features. If your team is near that line, price the Business plan now rather than after you have moved your pipeline in.

On Pro the monthly allowances are 1,000 campaign emails and 1,000 AI chats per user, 1,000 enrichment credits for the whole workspace (per workspace on the table re-read 11 November 2026), and one connected mailbox per user. A single rep running cold outreach from SoftSync can reach 1,000 campaign emails well before the month ends, and the page does not say what happens when you do, whether sending stops or an overage is charged. Ask before you plan a campaign around it.

Month-to-month billing costs about a third more than yearly: $39 against $29 on Pro, $79 against $59 on Business. There is no free plan, and the pricing page does not state a trial length; it says the checkout shows any trial terms. SoftSync's own home page says it has no integrations directory and instead gives your AI agent a way in through the API and MCP access; if your stack depends on ready-made connectors, check the specific ones on the integrations page before you commit. We found no independent buyer reviews we could read, so the only voices on the site are the testimonials SoftSync chose, most of them from founders and investors rather than daily users.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Pro, per seat · per seat a month billed yearly
pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-26 on softsync.ai/pricing in a headless browser, including the plan table and every pricing FAQ answer; re-read 2026-11-11 on softsync.ai/pricing and softsync.ai/pricing.md, amounts unchanged) Two standard paid plans, priced per seat per month, plus a custom Enterprise tier; there is no free plan. Pro is $29 per seat a month billed yearly or $39 billed monthly, and Business is $59 per seat a month billed yearly or $79 monthly; the page says yearly billing saves about 25%, and its FAQ says prices exclude VAT. Enterprise is custom-priced. Both paid plans carry the same feature set: flexible records and custom objects, table, pipeline and calendar views, email sync, campaigns and templates, meeting notes and summaries, a desktop recorder and Chrome extension, reports and dashboards, the AI Assistant, Autopilot workflows, record and contact enrichment, integrations, API and MCP access. What changes is capacity: Pro allows at most 5 team members and 10 groups per workspace, 250,000 records per table and 1 mailbox connection per user, with 1,000 campaign emails and 1,000 chats per user per calendar month and 1,000 enrichment credits a month (the table re-read 11 November 2026 labels the enrichment row per workspace, under a heading that says per user, so plan on one shared pool); Business raises those to 25 team members, 100 groups, 1,000,000 records, 5 mailboxes and 10,000 of each monthly allowance, and adds Priority Support for data migration and a workspace consultant, which are self-served on Pro. The page also lists prices in EUR, GBP, AUD, CAD, NZD, CHF, DKK, SEK, NOK and ISK. It publishes no trial length: the FAQ says the checkout page shows any trial terms and whether payment details are needed. Early-stage teams can ask about startup pricing on a call.

compare_with.name: folk
compare_with.why: folk is the closest comparison in our own dossiers: also a lightweight, per-seat CRM for small teams that dislike heavyweight sales software. On folk's published prices (re-verified 3 September 2026) Standard is $24 per member a month billed yearly or $30 monthly, against SoftSync Pro at $29 or $39, so folk is the cheaper entry by $5 to $9 a seat. folk also states its trial openly, two weeks without a credit card, where SoftSync's pricing page leaves it to the checkout. SoftSync puts more of the sales day inside the one plan: email campaigns, meeting notes and summaries, a desktop recorder, Autopilot workflows and MCP access for AI assistants are all on Pro, and its enrichment allowance is 1,000 credits a month for the workspace (per workspace on the table re-read 11 November 2026) against folk's 500 on Standard. folk has no five-person ceiling on its entry plan. A team that mainly manages relationships and contacts fits folk; a team of five or fewer that wants outreach, meetings and automation in one place, and wants an AI assistant to act on the records, fits SoftSync.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested SoftSync on its 14 day Business trial, which needs no card: a CSV of 20 test contacts was mapped by the AI step in about 20 s and imported in about 40 s, with 20 valid and 0 invalid rows, but the Record Matching default (First Name) would have merged all 20 rows, so it had to be changed to Emails. The imported deal stage lands in the contact field Lifecycle Stage and not in Deals, so a Kanban view Lead pipeline was made, which was ready about 5 min after the start. The MCP page offers only an OAuth connection and was not connected, so working from Claude or ChatGPT directly was not tested. An API key could be made without payment. The USD prices match our dossier, but the Business plan card in the app lists 5.000 AI chats, emails and enrichments a month where the public pricing page says 10,000, and the trial gives 200 enrichment credits. No checkout was opened and nothing was paid. Account and start: the account was created by us, who was signed in at app.softsync.ai in his Chrome; our AI assistant ran the test in its own tab, starting at 13:59 with the onboarding. The interface was already on English (US). The onboarding filled a test name into the profile of the account (a made up name) and a made up company Sample Snowboards with the website example.com; the profile name was not changed back. The dossier name is SoftSync and the review is on MSS (softsync-review). The pain that was tested: manual CRM updates, wanting Claude or ChatGPT to work in the CRM directly. Onboarding: workspace set-up with a name, a website (the app read example.com and showed a card Example Domain, changed to the company name), a role (Sales), a team size (2-10), Invite your teammates (Not now), How did you hear about us (Website), a skipped story, Where are your contacts today (Spreadsheet), Bring your contacts in, Connect your email and calendar (Skip for now, the Connect email button was not used) and You're all set. No card, phone number or password was asked. Core action: import of a made up test file test-contacten-20.csv (1.4 KB, 20 contacts) via Import a spreadsheet, Contacts, Separate files. The step AI is analyzing your headers took about 20 s and mapped first_name, last_name, email, company, title and phone by itself; the column deal_stage went to Contacts, Lifecycle Stage and deal_value to Companies, Revenue. Review & Validate Data said 20 valid, 0 invalid of 20 rows; the step Map Field Options mapped 6 of 6 stage values (Contacted, Lost, New, Proposal, Qualified, Won) as new options. Pitfall: Record Matching for Contacts was set to First Name by default; all 20 rows have the first name Test, which would have merged them, so Emails was chosen. The import said Import started! Importing 40 records (20 contacts and 20 company rows), took about 40 s and ended with Your data has been successfully imported. Contacts then showed 25 in view (20 imported and 5 sample contacts marked [SAMPLE]) and Companies 20 companies. Pipeline: the Deals group already has a standard Pipeline view with the stages New, Qualification, Proposal, Negotiation, Won and Lost and three sample deals. The imported contacts do not land in Deals, so a new view Lead pipeline was made in Contacts (Kanban, group by Lifecycle Stage): New 5, Contacted 4, Qualified 4, Customer 0, Lost 1, Proposal 4, Won 2 and No Status 5 (the sample contacts), 20 of 20 imported contacts. The standard Deals pipeline was visible about 4 min after the start and the own contact pipeline was ready about 5 min after the start; the import and the pipeline took about 25 clicks. MCP: Settings, MCP shows Set up MCP with your AI assistant with the buttons Set up in ChatGPT, Set up in Claude and Set up in Grok, the MCP server address https://api.softsync.ai/mcp/softsync and the text This connection uses OAuth. The assistant will open a sign-in page so you can approve access without sharing an API key. It also says Access follows your SoftSync permissions, Review write actions before approving and Only connect trusted servers. No plan limit was seen on the page. Under Agent skills there are 18 fixed prompts, for example Fill in the missing Emails on 20 records in Companies. The connection itself was NOT made: it needs an OAuth sign-in with an outside account, which was not allowed, so Claude or ChatGPT working in the CRM directly was not tested. API key: Settings, API keys, Create a key, the name My integration and Set it up worked without any payment and showed It's live. Copy your key now: you won't see it again. The key was not written down, is masked in the screenshot and was not used. It was then revoked with the bin icon (Revoke API Key ... This action cannot be undone) and the list said No API keys found again. There is also a tab OAuth Apps. Plans: The plans were read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 in the app (Settings, Billing, Change plan, in USD) and read again just before this delivery the same day on the public page softsync.ai/pricing with the currency set to USD, with the same amounts. Pro: $29.00 per seat a month when billed yearly ($348.00 a year for 1 seat) and $39.00 when billed monthly; up to 5 seats, 10 groups and 1 mailbox per user. Business: $59.00 per seat a month when billed yearly ($708.00 a year for 1 seat) and $79.00 when billed monthly; up to 25 seats, 100 groups and 5 mailboxes per user. The switch says Yearly (-25%). Enterprise is on request. The public pricing table lists, per user a month, 1,000 campaign emails, chats and enrichment credits on Pro and 10,000 of each on Business. Trial: Settings, Billing says Your plan: Business, Trial, Seats 1 seat(s), Billing Not chosen yet, Price Free until 2 dec 2026 and Trial ends 2 dec 2026. That is a trial of 14 days on the Business plan from 18 Nov 2026 and no card was asked. The credits in the trial are Enrichment 200 (renews 2 dec), AI chats 5,000, Campaign emails 10,000 and Text messages 120 (renews 1 dec). The partner offer of 30 days came through our partner link and this account did not use that link, so the standard trial applied. Differences against the dossier: (a) the public pricing page lists 10,000 chats, campaign emails and enrichment credits a month for Business, while the plan card in the app says 5.000 AI chats, emails and enrichments a month for Business (and the Credits panel shows 5,000 chats, 10,000 campaign emails and 200 enrichment credits); (b) the dossier gives no trial length, while the app gave a trial until 2 dec 2026 on Business without a card; (c) the dossier lists 1,000 enrichment credits a month on Pro, while the trial shows 200 enrichment credits. The USD prices themselves are unchanged. Checkout: no checkout was opened, the plan buttons were not clicked, no card was asked and no tax or total was shown, so no price at checkout is known. Cancelling: Settings, Organization, Danger Zone has Delete Organization (Once you delete a organization, there is no going back. Please be certain.), which was not clicked. Billing has no separate cancel button; going lower is Downgrade to Pro. Because there is no card, the trial runs out without a charge on the page, which was not tested further. Not tested: Claude or ChatGPT working in the CRM through MCP, the e-mail and calendar connection, campaigns, meeting notes, Autopilot, cancelling itself, and the audiences Sales teams about to hire a sixth rep and Outbound reps sending heavy cold email. Clean up: the account and the test data stay: the organization Sample Snowboards, 20 test contacts, 20 test companies and the view Lead pipeline in Contacts; the profile name stays on the made up name from the onboarding; the API key was revoked; nothing was connected; the empty tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The import wizard keeps First Name as the matching field for contacts by default, which merges people who share a first name; check it before you start. A deal stage column in your file does not become a deal: it lands in a contact field, so you need your own view if you want a pipeline of imported leads. The plan card for Business shows lower monthly allowances than the public pricing page, and the trial gives only 200 enrichment credits, so check the numbers in your own Billing page. There is no separate cancel button; the only end is Delete Organization in the Danger Zone, and the trial has no card.

The step AI is analyzing your headers took about 20 s and mapped first_name, last_name, email, company, title and phone by itself; the column deal_stage went to Contacts, Lifecycle Stage and deal_value to Companies, Revenue. Review & Validate Data said 20 valid, 0 invalid of 20 rows; the step Map Field Options mapped 6 of 6 stage values (Contacted, Lost, New, Proposal, Qualified, Won) as new options. Pitfall: Record Matching for Contacts was set to First Name by default; all 20 rows have the first name Test, which would have merged them, so Emails was chosen. The import said Import started! Importing 40 records (20 contacts and 20 company rows), took about 40 s and ended with Your data has been successfully imported. Contacts then showed 25 in view (20 imported and 5 sample contacts marked [SAMPLE]) and Companies 20 companies. Pipeline: the Deals group already has a standard Pipeline view with the stages New, Qualification, Proposal, Negotiation, Won and Lost and three sample deals. The imported contacts do not land in Deals, so a new view Lead pipeline was made in Contacts (Kanban, group by Lifecycle Stage): New 5, Contacted 4, Qualified 4, Customer 0, Lost 1, Proposal 4, Won 2 and No Status 5 (the sample contacts), 20 of 20 imported contacts. The standard Deals pipeline was visible about 4 min after the start and the own contact pipeline was ready about 5 min after the start; the import and the pipeline took about 25 clicks. MCP: Settings, MCP shows Set up MCP with your AI assistant with the buttons Set up in ChatGPT, Set up in Claude and Set up in Grok, the MCP server address https://api.softsync.ai/mcp/softsync and the text This connection uses OAuth. The assistant will open a sign-in page so you can approve access without sharing an API key. It also says Access follows your SoftSync permissions, Review write actions before approving and Only connect trusted servers. No plan limit was seen on the page. Under Agent skills there are 18 fixed prompts, for example Fill in the missing Emails on 20 records in Companies. The connection itself was NOT made: it needs an OAuth sign-in with an outside account, which was not allowed, so Claude or ChatGPT working in the CRM directly was not tested. API key: Settings, API keys, Create a key, the name My integration and Set it up worked without any payment and showed It's live. Copy your key now: you won't see it again. The key was not written down, is masked in the screenshot and was not used. It was then revoked with the bin icon (Revoke API Key ... This action cannot be undone) and the list said No API keys found again. There is also a tab OAuth Apps. Plans: The plans were read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 in the app (Settings, Billing, Change plan, in USD) and read again just before this delivery the same day on the public page softsync.ai/pricing with the currency set to USD, with the same amounts. Pro: $29.00 per seat a month when billed yearly ($348.00 a year for 1 seat) and $39.00 when billed monthly; up to 5 seats, 10 groups and 1 mailbox per user. Business: $59.00 per seat a month when billed yearly ($708.00 a year for 1 seat) and $79.00 when billed monthly; up to 25 seats, 100 groups and 5 mailboxes per user. The switch says Yearly (-25%). Enterprise is on request. The public pricing table lists, per user a month, 1,000 campaign emails, chats and enrichment credits on Pro and 10,000 of each on Business. Trial: Settings, Billing says Your plan: Business, Trial, Seats 1 seat(s), Billing Not chosen yet, Price Free until 2 dec 2026 and Trial ends 2 dec 2026. That is a trial of 14 days on the Business plan from 18 Nov 2026 and no card was asked. The credits in the trial are Enrichment 200 (renews 2 dec), AI chats 5,000, Campaign emails 10,000 and Text messages 120 (renews 1 dec). Differences against the dossier: (a) the public pricing page lists 10,000 chats, campaign emails and enrichment credits a month for Business, while the plan card in the app says 5.000 AI chats, emails and enrichments a month for Business (and the Credits panel shows 5,000 chats, 10,000 campaign emails and 200 enrichment credits); (b) the dossier gives no trial length, while the app gave a trial until 2 dec 2026 on Business without a card; (c) the dossier lists 1,000 enrichment credits a month on Pro, while the trial shows 200 enrichment credits. Billing has no separate cancel button; going lower is Downgrade to Pro. Because there is no card, the trial runs out without a charge on the page, which was not tested further. Clean up: the account and the test data stay: the organization Sample Snowboards, 20 test contacts, 20 test companies and the view Lead pipeline in Contacts; the profile name stays on the made up name from the onboarding; the API key was revoked; nothing was connected; the empty tab was closed. No kit records were entered. A check of this export route with synthetic records, on the account and date stated. Re-importing the export was not tested. claim_checks.observed: The onboarding went from the workspace set-up to Open my workspace without a card, phone number or password. The e-mail and calendar connection was offered and skipped with Skip for now; nothing was connected.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The onboarding screens against our own walk through them; the mailbox connection itself was not tried.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: You can start and fill a workspace without connecting a mailbox or entering payment details.

claim_checks.observed: The Pro card says up to 5 seats and 10 groups, with 1 mailbox per user, which matches the plan limits in our dossier and on the public pricing table. Only 1 seat was used in this test.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The plan card on the Billing page against the dossier and the public pricing table; a second seat was not added.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A team of five or fewer fits on Pro by the plan card; a sixth seat is above that limit; the limit itself was not tried.

claim_checks.observed: The made up file of 20 contacts was analysed by the AI header step in about 20 s, validated as 20 valid and 0 invalid of 20 rows, and imported with the message Importing 40 records in about 40 s (20 contacts and 20 company rows); Contacts then showed 25 in view with the 5 sample contacts.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The counts in the wizard and in the Contacts and Companies lists against the 20 rows of our own file; a larger or messier file was not tried.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A small spreadsheet comes in within a minute or two with the columns mapped for you.

claim_checks.observed: Record Matching for Contacts was set to First Name by default. All 20 rows of the test file have the same first name, so that setting would have merged them; Emails was chosen by hand.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The default setting in the wizard has no counterpart in our dossier; it was changed before the import, so the merge itself was not seen.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: Check the matching field before you import, because the default can merge people who share a first name.

claim_checks.observed: The deal stage column went to the contact field Lifecycle Stage, not to Deals. A Kanban view Lead pipeline was made in Contacts grouped by Lifecycle Stage: New 5, Contacted 4, Qualified 4, Customer 0, Lost 1, Proposal 4, Won 2 and No Status 5 (the sample contacts), 20 of 20 imported contacts. It took about 5 min and about 25 clicks from the start to this view.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: Our count of the stage columns against the 20 rows of the file; the dossier has no statement about how stages from a file are imported, and the clicks and minutes are our own set-up times.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: Imported stages do not become deals; for a pipeline of imported leads you make your own view in Contacts, which is quick but is a step you must know about.

claim_checks.observed: The MCP page shows the server address https://api.softsync.ai/mcp/softsync with the text that the connection uses OAuth and the buttons Set up in ChatGPT, Set up in Claude and Set up in Grok. No plan limit was seen on the page. Nothing was connected, because it needs an OAuth sign-in with an outside account.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The settings page against a test that did not connect an assistant; the 18 fixed prompts under Agent skills were not run.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: You can see how the connection is set up, but whether Claude or ChatGPT really works in the CRM is not confirmed by this test.

claim_checks.observed: An API key named My integration was created with Create a key and Set it up without any payment, on the Business trial, and the dialog said It's live. The key is masked in the screenshot, was not used and was revoked afterwards; the list said No API keys found again.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The key list before and after the revoke against the dossier line that API access comes with a paid plan; the key was never used for a request.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: API access is open on the trial and a key can be removed again at once; whether a key works on a paid Pro plan was not tried.

claim_checks.observed: The plan card shows Pro at $29.00 per seat a month billed yearly ($348.00 a year for 1 seat) and Business at $59.00 ($708.00 a year); the monthly prices are $39.00 and $79.00. The public pricing page in USD gave the same amounts. They match the dossier.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The Change plan prices in the app and the public pricing page against the dossier; tax was not shown and no checkout was opened.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The seat prices are as listed: Pro $29 and Business $59 a month when paid yearly, $39 and $79 when paid monthly, per seat.

claim_checks.claim: 5.000 AI chats, emails and enrichments a month
claim_checks.observed: The Business plan card says 5.000 AI chats, emails and enrichments a month. The public pricing page and our dossier list 10,000 a month for Business. The Credits panel of the trial shows 5,000 AI chats and 10,000 campaign emails.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The wording on the plan card against the 10,000 on the public pricing page and in the dossier; the allowances were not used up.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The plan card for Business shows half the monthly allowance that the public pricing page lists, so check your own Billing page before you size a team on Business.

claim_checks.observed: The trial Credits panel shows Enrichment credits 200 for the month, renewing 2 dec. The dossier lists 1,000 enrichment credits a month on Pro and the public pricing table lists 1,000 on Pro and 10,000 on Business.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The trial credit figure against the dossier and the public table; a paid plan was not opened, so its real allowance was not seen.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: During the Business trial you get fewer enrichment credits than either paid plan lists, so the trial does not show the full allowance.

claim_checks.observed: The Billing page says Business, Trial, Billing Not chosen yet, Price Free until 2 dec 2026 and Trial ends 2 dec 2026, which is a trial of 14 days from 18 Nov 2026, and no card was asked. The dossier gives no trial length. The partner offer of 30 days did not apply because the account did not use our partner link.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The trial dates on the Billing page against a dossier without a trial length; what happens on 2 dec 2026 was not tested.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The standard trial is 14 days on Business without a card; a longer trial only comes through the partner offer.

claim_checks.observed: Settings, Organization, Danger Zone shows Delete Organization with the text that there is no going back; it was not clicked. Billing has no separate cancel button, only Downgrade to Pro, and there is no card on the trial.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The Danger Zone and Billing page against a test that did not delete or pay anything.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The only visible way to end the account is to delete the organization; cancelling a paid plan was not seen because nothing was bought.

claim_checks.observed: No checkout was opened and no plan button was clicked; the Billing page shows the trial price and the plan prices, but no tax, fee or total at checkout was shown, and no card was asked.
claim_checks.plan: 14 day Business trial without a card; no checkout was opened, nothing was paid
claim_checks.comparability: The plan page prices against a checkout that was not opened; no tax line, fee or stored cost rule could be compared.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: What you pay at checkout, with tax and the seat minimum, is not known from this test.

The partner offer of 30 days came through our partner link and this account did not use that link, so the standard trial applied. Differences against the dossier: (a) the public pricing page lists 10,000 chats, campaign emails and enrichment credits a month for Business, while the plan card in the app says 5.000 AI chats, emails and enrichments a month for Business (and the Credits panel shows 5,000 chats, 10,000 campaign emails and 200 enrichment credits); (b) the dossier gives no trial length, while the app gave a trial until 2 dec 2026 on Business without a card; (c) the dossier lists 1,000 enrichment credits a month on Pro, while the trial shows 200 enrichment credits. The USD prices themselves are unchanged. Checkout: no checkout was opened, the plan buttons were not clicked, no card was asked and no tax or total was shown, so no price at checkout is known. Cancelling: Settings, Organization, Danger Zone has Delete Organization (Once you delete a organization, there is no going back. Please be certain.), which was not clicked. Billing has no separate cancel button; going lower is Downgrade to Pro. Because there is no card, the trial runs out without a charge on the page, which was not tested further. Not tested: Claude or ChatGPT working in the CRM through MCP, the e-mail and calendar connection, campaigns, meeting notes, Autopilot, cancelling itself, and the audiences Sales teams about to hire a sixth rep and Outbound reps sending heavy cold email. Clean up: the account and the test data stay: the organization Sample Snowboards, 20 test contacts, 20 test companies and the view Lead pipeline in Contacts; the profile name stays on the made up name from the onboarding; the API key was revoked; nothing was connected; the empty tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The import wizard keeps First Name as the matching field for contacts by default, which merges people who share a first name; check it before you start. A deal stage column in your file does not become a deal: it lands in a contact field, so you need your own view if you want a pipeline of imported leads. The plan card for Business shows lower monthly allowances than the public pricing page, and the trial gives only 200 enrichment credits, so check the numbers in your own Billing page. There is no separate cancel button; the only end is Delete Organization in the Danger Zone, and the trial has no card.
